hints.content: The *domain* of a function is the set of all inputs for which the function is defined.

According to the graph, $f$ is defined for all inputs between $-5$ and $6$, including both $-5$ and $6$. This means we can write the domain of $f$ as $-5 \leq x \leq 6$.

options.explanation: In most cases outside of this exercise, an image will only show part of the complete graph of a function, so unless we're given further information about the function, we will not be able to tell exactly what the domain of the function is.
options.showPrompt: Can we always tell the domain of a function from its graph?

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The graph of the function f starts at the point negative five, zero and increases at a non linear rate to negative three, two. Then it decreases at a non linear rate to negative one, zero. It continues to decrease, but the rate slows until one, negative two. Then it increases at a non linear rate until three, zero. A line segment connects three, zero to six, six, which is plotted. There is a solid horizontal line from negative five, zero to six, zero. Both points are plotted. There is a dotted vertical line from six, zero to six, six.

hints.content: In conclusion, the domain of the function is $-5 \leq x \leq 6$.
